ky_arsenal_the.blurb: A steep, heavily featured wall in Muir Valley, in the Rogers area of the Red River Gorge. The orange rock is peppered with pockets, edges and big huecos, and the face leans well past vertical. Most of the ten lines are sport, with a pair of trad routes mixed in. Difficulty sits at the upper end: a couple of easier lines in the 5.8 to 5.9 range, then mostly 5.11 and 5.12 pump-fests. The south-facing orientation makes it a good pick for cold or damp winter days, while summer afternoons here turn sweaty. It is a destination for climbers already comfortable on steep, sustained ground rather than a beginner crag.

ky_great_arch_the.blurb: A small sector of Muir Valley in the Red River Gorge near Rogers, holding about ten routes, mostly sport with two trad lines. The grade spread starts around 5.8 and tops out in the 5.13 range, with the middle of the range, 5.11 and 5.12, holding most of the lines. Muir Valley as a whole is known for sport climbing on grades that feel generous, and this sector fits that pattern for climbers who want a short list of moderately hard to hard lines away from the busiest walls.

ky_b_hole_wall.blurb: A wall on the shaded side of Hole in the Wall, in the Bald Rock part of the Red River Gorge. It is the first cliff reached along the shady branch of the trail. Sun hits the face only in the early morning, until around ten, and after that it stays in shade, which makes it a comfortable choice from spring through fall. Of the ten lines, eight are sport and two are trad. A few moderates in the 5.7 to 5.8 range share the wall with a handful of 5.10s and several steeper, overhung 5.11 and 5.12 lines on pockets.

ky_unholey_wall_the.blurb: A sport-only wall at Hole in the Wall in the Bald Rock area of the Red River Gorge. It is a short walk along the trail past the neighboring A-Hole wall, starting with a short golden face. Shade lasts until roughly one or two in the afternoon, then it can get hot when the sun is out, since there is less leaf cover here. The ten routes run from about 5.9 up to the 5.13 range, and most of them fall in the 5.11 and 5.12 band, so it suits climbers with some experience on bolted lines who want a wall that is quiet and shaded in the morning.

ky_patterson.blurb: A sport crag along the Inner Loop Trail at the Cathedral Domain in the southern Red River Gorge, and the second wall you reach on that loop. It has a lower tier and a taller upper tier that holds most of the lines. The ten routes span roughly 5.8 to 5.12, with half of them at 5.11, so there are a few warm-ups and a solid block of harder climbs. Because the range is broad, it works well for a mixed group. The wall stays in shade most of the day, though some seepage means it needs about a day to dry after heavy rain.
